SMS Schmidt Motorsport: Konrad Schmidt's squad runs Audi's works V8 quattros and carries the number 1 of reigning champion Hans-Joachim Stuck.
AZR Audi Zentrum Reutlingen: A new second Audi team for 1991, fielding Frank Jelinski and Frank Biela in V8 quattros.
BMW M Team Schnitzer: BMW's lead M3 squad, with Johnny Cecotto, Joachim Winkelhock and Kris Nissen on Yokohama tyres.
BMW M Team Bigazzi: The Italian BMW squad led by Steve Soper, one of the fastest M3 crews in the field.
AMG Mercedes: Hans-Werner Aufrecht's Affalterbach outfit builds the Mercedes engines and runs the strongest 190E Evo IIs on exclusive Bridgestones.
Zakspeed Racing: Erich Zakowski's experienced team runs works-supported Mercedes for Roland Asch and guests including a young Michael Schumacher.
Snobeck Racing: Dany Snobeck's French Mercedes team pairs former Formula 1 winner Jacques Laffite with Alain Cudini.
MS-Jet Racing: A Mercedes team with works-loaned cars for Jörg van Ommen and Frank Schmickler.
Linder M Team: A long-standing BMW privateer squad fielding up to three M3s.
MM Diebels Alt: The brewery-backed BMW team led by former Formula 1 driver Christian Danner.
Unitron Sports: BMW privateers led by Peter Zakowski, a contender for the private-driver ITR Cup.
Tic Tac Tauber Team: Tauber Motorsport's BMW M3 in green and white Tic Tac colours.
Auto Maass Climair Team: A single-car BMW privateer entry for Kurt König.
Marlboro BMW Dealer Team: A Dutch BMW dealer entry for Cor Euser.
Opel Team Eggenberger: Ruedi Eggenberger's Swiss team runs the Opel Omega 3000 Evo 500 on Michelins.
Opel Team Irmscher: Opel's development partner fields the Omega for Volker Strycek and Franz Engstler.
Gerd Ruch Motorsport: The thundering Ford Mustang 5.0 GT, the only American V8 in the field.
